title: API tokens
intro: Tokens let scripts, monitoring and the hostashi command line use the API as you. Each has its own scopes, sites and lifetime, and you can revoke each one on its own.
introAdmin: Where tokens are accepted from is set under Firewall.
revokeText: Everything that uses {{prefix}}… stops working at once. This cannot be undone.
none: No tokens yet. Create one with New token.

create.title: New API token
create.name: Name
create.nameHint: What uses it, for example “Uptime monitoring” or “Deploy from CI”. Up to 64 characters.

secret.title: Save this token now
secret.text: Hostashi stores only a hash of “{{name}}” and cannot show it again. If it is lost, revoke it and create a new one.
secret.copyFailed: Copying is not possible here. Select the token and copy it by hand.
secret.neverExpires: This token never expires. Revoke it when the job that uses it ends.
secret.highRiskKeep: . Keep it where only you can read it.
secret.use: Send it as <code1>Authorization: Bearer …</code1>, or give it to the command line with <code2>hostashi login -token {{origin}}</code2> on stdin.

grant.allSites: Every site I can reach, also later ones
grant.noSites: You cannot reach any site yet.
grant.daysHint: 1 to 365. The token stops working after that.
grant.unlimitedHint: Only for a monitoring or deploy job you look after.
grant.unlimitedTitle: This token works until you revoke it
grant.unlimitedText: If it leaks, it stays usable for as long as nobody notices. Prefer a lifetime and renew it.

allowlist.intro: Addresses API tokens are accepted from, one IP address or CIDR range per line. An empty list accepts them from anywhere. This is not a firewall rule: it applies at once, to every account's tokens, and logins in the browser keep working. The server itself (127.0.0.1 and ::1) is always allowed, so the hostashi command on it keeps working.
allowlist.label: Allowed addresses
allowlist.savedList: Saved. Tokens now work only from these addresses and the server itself.

device.title: Log in a device
device.intro: Approve the code that hostashi login shows in your terminal.
device.approvedText: Return to your terminal: the CLI has its token within a few seconds. You can see and revoke the token under Your account.
device.denied: Login denied. The CLI gets no token.
device.warnTitle: Approve only a login you started yourself
device.warnText: Whoever started it gets an API token for your account. If you did not just run hostashi login, deny it.

errors.not_found: No login is waiting for this code. Check it, or run hostashi login again: a code is valid for ten minutes.
errors.rate_limited: Too many wrong codes. Wait a few minutes and try again.
errors.too_many_tokens: You have too many API tokens. Revoke one first.
You have 100 working API tokens, the most there can be. Revoke one first.
errors.second_factor_required: Set up a second factor (TOTP or a passkey) before you create a token.
errors.not_found: This token does not exist any more. Reload the page.
